router_distinctions:
Pick the tier that best balances capability and cost for the task. Do not default to the cheapest option — choose the right tool for the job.

Low-priority tiers: simple direct actions (greetings, lookups, quick answers). Mid-priority tiers: investigation, analysis, code changes, debugging, multi-step work. High-priority tiers: architecture, deep reasoning, large-scale refactoring.

CRITICAL: The 'agent' tier spawns multiple AI agents in parallel — ONLY use it for tasks with independent parallel workstreams. Most tasks, even complex ones, should go to a single-model tier.

tiers.name: haiku
tiers.router_label: Casual conversation, simple factual questions, short summaries, translations, web searches, running scheduled jobs, toggling settings, simple file reads, quick edits

tiers.name: sonnet
tiers.router_label: Code review, debugging, investigating issues, reading logs, understanding system behavior, explaining complex concepts, research synthesis, editing code files, implementing features, fixing bugs, creating scripts, writing tests, multi-file changes, create scheduled jobs, create reminders, multi-step tasks that a single developer can handle sequentially

tiers.name: opus
tiers.router_label: Architecture design, system-level reasoning, complex trade-off analysis, large-scale refactoring, implementing complex features, redesigning system architecture, building new modules from scratch, complex multi-step tasks requiring deep thinking

tiers.name: agent
tiers.router_label: ONLY for tasks explicitly requesting a team of agents, or requiring parallel independent workstreams that CANNOT be done sequentially by one model (e.g. 'build a full app with frontend + backend + tests simultaneously', 'write 5 articles at once', 'research 3 topics in parallel'). If one model can handle it step-by-step, use sonnet or opus instead.
